bull_bear.body: Debt expected to increase sequentially by INR 200-250 mn in FY27 to fund capex; Working capital cycle improved to 179 days (from 194), targeting 160 days by FY27 end; Cash flow from operations up to INR 1,424 mn.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Geopolitical volatility affecting feedstock/logistics (though currently beneficial for pricing); Execution risk on Site 5 commissioning; Working capital intensity during ramp-up; Fire incident at external warehouse (INR 70 mn loss).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly confident; Emphasizes 'golden age' for Indian specialty chemicals; Focus on execution and scaling complex chemistry; Strategic hiring (ex-Bayer/ALTANA) to open new frontiers in material science.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Management explicitly states geopolitical conflict has driven unprecedented pricing power (>20%) which they believe is sustainable for 2-3 quarters; Shift to selling via Indian subsidiaries of MNCs temporarily reduced direct exports but is reversing; New 'Integrated Polymerizations' competency is a stealth entry into high-barrier oil & gas additives.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Borrowings as at 30 June 2026: INR 4,215 million of working capital loans and INR 1,000 million of term loans (the deck states the two components; it does not state a total).
- Working capital: "Debtor days reduced on the back of aggressive collections, and inventory days reduced marginally. The overall working capital cycle is marginally lower than at March 2026."
- The deck discloses no dividend policy, buyback or equity-raise plan.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: LSM (Large-Scale Mfg): 43% of sales, pricing +20% YoY, +18% QoQ in Q4. CRAMS + CEM: 55% of revenue, targeting 70%+ by FY30. Pharma+Agro: 46% of mix. Material Science: 17% (growing with Site 3++). Site 4 revenue grew 4x to INR 220 cr (21% of total).
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Supply disruption of ethylene/propylene derivatives and logistics bottlenecks have tightened global supply. | Aether Industries Limited | beneficiary | High | Direct beneficiary of >20% price increases in LSM segment; Site 5 commissioning aligns with peak demand; Open cost-plus models protect margins while competitors face feedstock issues. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Three business verticals: CRAMS (Contract Research and Manufacturing Services), CEM (Contract and Exclusive Manufacturing) and LSM (Large Scale Manufacturing); "CRAMS and CEM together now contribute 60% of revenue".
- Stated mix ambition: "We expect these two verticals to reach 70% over the next couple of years, notwithstanding the new products being launched in the Large Scale Manufacturing (LSM) vertical."
- Sectoral spread of quarterly revenue from operations: pharmaceutical 32.2%, oil and gas 31.4%, material science 16.6%, agrochemical 9.5% — "The portfolio remains well diversified across sectors."
- Deliberate de-concentration in R&D: "over 65 live projects, of which 70% are in non-pharmaceutical and non-agrochemical sectors".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Site renaming] Sites have been renamed: Site 1 -> Catalyst (CRAMS); Site 2 -> Genesis (LSM/CEM); Site 3 and Site 3++ -> Ascend (LSM/CEM); Site 4 -> Strata (CEM); Site 5 and Site 5+ -> Magnum (LSM/CEM).
- [Guidance] "We maintain our guidance of approximately 30% EBITDA margin for FY2027."
- [Named counterparties] The deck names Baker Hughes (quarterly revenue of INR 700 million, dedicated plant Strata), Milliken & Company / Milliken Chemical and Textile (India) (dedicated plant Ascend), Saudi Aramco (joint development of Converge Polyol) and an unnamed European major (CEM programme in material science, plus a further block at Magnum).
- [Milestone] Oil and gas revenue crossed INR 1,000 million for the quarter for the first time.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: FY26 EBITDA margin expanded to 31% from 28%; Q4 margins pressured by INR 70 mn fire provision and INR 10 mn year-end provisions; Open cost-plus P&L for CEM protects against raw material inflation; LSM seeing temporary margin delta from price hikes.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: No specific % given, driven by Site 3++, Site 4 ramp, and Site 5 Phase 1 commercialization in FY27. Margin: EBITDA 29-30%, PAT 19-20% expected for FY27. Order Inflow: Robust CRAMS pipeline converting to CEM. Capex: INR 3,000-3,500 mn for FY27 (Site 5 & new R&D).
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Validation batches completed for 3 new large-scale products (2 pharma, 1 agro) at Site 5 with orders in hand; Baker Hughes continuous orders (INR 76 mn in Q4); Strong visibility for Converge Polyols FY27.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Site 5 Phase 1 commissioning (May/Jun 2026); New R&D facility (2x capacity) by Q2 FY28; Semiconductor materials opportunity tripling by 2030 (initial 400 tonnes @ $40-50/kg); New 'Integrated Polymerizations' competency targeting Oil & Gas/Material Science.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Aether leveraged geopolitical disruptions to drive >20% pricing gains in its Large-Scale Manufacturing vertical while successfully transitioning toward a high-margin CRAMS/CEM model (55% of revenue) with Site 5 commissioning imminent. Despite Q4 one-offs (fire provision, lack of insurance claim income), the structural shift to complex chemistry and expanded R&D capacity positions the firm for sustained 29-30% EBITDA margins and triple-digit growth in semiconductor materials by 2030.

open.item: Otsuka Chemical contract on track, expected to achieve target of Rs.35-40 crores of sales in FY26.
Three new LSM products (2 pharma, 1 agrochemical) from Site 5 to be commissioned by May-end or first week of June; validation batches done and orders in hand.
Final fixed-asset claim for Nov-2023 fire submitted to surveyor, being assessed, with expectation to get settled by end of Q1 FY27; insurance exceptional item to end after FY27.
Total FY26 capex Rs.3,838 million (~Rs.384 cr); FY27 capex expected Rs.3,000-3,500 million (~Rs.300-350 cr), primarily Site 5 and new R&D site.
FY27 margins expected stable at 29-30% EBITDA and 19-20% PAT.
Working capital cycle reduced to 179 days (from 194 at Mar-25); expect ~160 days by end FY27 (try for 150).
QIP monies exhausted in Q3; debt (currently ~Rs.400 cr) to increase gradually and sequentially for project needs; ~Rs.200-250 crores additional debt expected by end FY27.
Core competencies moving from 8x8 towards 9x9 now and 10x10 for sure by end of this year (FY27).
FY27 growth drivers: Site 4 and Site 3+ (Milliken) ramp-up, new fume hoods/NMR projects, and commercialization of Site 5 Phase 1 in FY27; exports expected to recover to 50-60% of top line.

Interim R&D expansion (2 labs, 18 fume hoods incl. 5 engineering, 400 MHz NMR) completed, commercialization from Q2 FY27; new R&D wing (15 labs incl 5 engineering, ~140 fume hoods, 2x expansion) to be commissioned in Q2 FY28.
Sticking with expectation of 3-4 molecules of the size of Milliken from R&D pipeline panning out into significant contracts within 1 to 3 years.
Vision of 70% plus of revenues from CRAMS and CEM by fiscal year 2030 (FY26: CRAMS+CEM 55%).
Semiconductor materials opportunity expected to triple by 2030; first phase producing 400 tonnes of molecules at average price $40-$50 per kilo.

Site 5: 4 blocks constructed (2 ready to run, trials ongoing), digging started on other 4 blocks; total 16 blocks possible plus ~4 more on 15-acre Site 5+ (46 acres, ~20 blocks total); total remaining capex ~Rs.1,500-1,600 crores over next 4 years, asset turn 1.5-1.75x.
Site 3+ and 3++ combined (6,500 tons) full revenue potential of ~Rs.300 cr.
Effective tax rate is 25.168% for Aether Industries and 17.16% for Aether Specialty; blended rate expected to fall below 25% as Aether Specialty mix increases.
